page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.m1.medium is a general-purpose virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, requiring external network-attached storage for operating system deployment and data persistence.

A key technical characteristic of the ecs.m1.medium is its legacy CPU feature set. The underlying processor lacks support for advanced instruction sets, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX2, AVX-512), Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), and hardware-accelerated cryptography flags such as AES and SHA_NI. Additionally, virtualization extensions, hyper-threading flags, and advanced bit manipulation instructions are not exposed to the guest operating system.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation provides predictable compute performance for workloads that do not require specialized vector processing or cryptographic acceleration. The balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes this instance appropriate for standard general-purpose workloads, such as basic web serving, lightweight application servers, and development environments that rely on external database services.
